summary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment that would require government outlays not to exceed receipts unless debt finances the excess, cap outstanding debt at 105% of its current level unless states approve an increase, mandate presidential impoundment of funds if debt approaches the limit, and require a two-thirds vote in both houses of Congress for new or increased general revenue taxes.

scores.thoughts: This bill proposes a constitutional amendment that would limit total government outlays to not exceed total receipts, effectively mandating a balanced budget unless debt is issued under strict conditions. It also includes provisions for impoundment of expenditures if debt limits are approached, directly aiming to reduce or control government spending.

The bill includes a provision requiring a two-thirds roll call vote in both Houses of Congress for any new or increased general revenue tax, making it harder to raise taxes. It also mentions an exception for a new end-user sales tax replacing existing income taxes, indicating a potential shift in tax policy.

The core of this bill is to propose a constitutional amendment directly related to the public debt. It sets limits on outstanding debt, establishes a process for increasing authorized debt that requires state approval, and mandates presidential impoundment of expenditures if debt limits are approached, all aimed at prioritizing debt reduction and control.

The bill is a proposed constitutional amendment that mandates total outlays shall not exceed total receipts unless financed by strictly limited authorized debt, caps outstanding debt at 105% of current levels with state-legislature approval required for any increase, requires presidential impoundment to enforce the cap, and imposes a two-thirds vote for new general revenue taxes. These provisions are the sole and entire purpose of the joint resolution.
